coreIdea.en: The Zero Conditional is a vending machine: put in the same coin, always get the same result — no exceptions, no doubt, no future tense involved.
coreIdea.es: El condicional cero es una máquina expendedora: metes la misma moneda y siempre sale el mismo resultado — sin excepciones, sin duda, y sin tiempo futuro.

text.en: Formula: If + Present Simple, Present Simple. Both halves stay in the present — like a machine that has no other setting. Use it for scientific facts, general truths, habits, and instructions: whenever the result is guaranteed, every single time.
text.es: Fórmula: If + presente simple, presente simple. Las dos mitades se quedan en presente — como una máquina que no tiene otro modo. Se usa para hechos científicos, verdades generales, hábitos e instrucciones: cuando el resultado está garantizado, siempre.

text.en: You can flip the order: 'If you heat ice, it melts' = 'Ice melts if you heat it.' Only add a comma when 'if' opens the sentence.
text.es: Puedes invertir el orden: 'If you heat ice, it melts' = 'Ice melts if you heat it.' Solo pones coma cuando 'if' abre la frase.

text.en: The #1 error: adding 'will' anywhere in a Zero Conditional. ❌ 'If you heat water, it will boil.' The machine has no future setting — it's always true, right now and every time. ✅ 'If you heat water, it boils.'
text.es: El error #1: meter 'will' en cualquier parte del condicional cero. ❌ 'If you heat water, it will boil.' La máquina no tiene modo futuro — es siempre cierto, ahora y en todo momento. ✅ 'If you heat water, it boils.'

examples.en: If you heat ice, it melts.
examples.es: Si calientas el hielo, se derrite.

examples.en: If people don't eat, they get hungry.
examples.es: Si las personas no comen, les da hambre.

examples.en: Plants die if they don't get water.
examples.es: Las plantas se mueren si no reciben agua.

examples.en: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
examples.es: Si mezclas azul y amarillo, obtienes verde.

examples.en: If the alarm rings, everyone leaves the building.
examples.es: Si suena la alarma, todos salen del edificio.

title.en: First Conditional — the real fork ahead
title.es: Primer condicional — la bifurcación real más adelante

coreIdea.en: The First Conditional stands you at a fork in the road that genuinely lies ahead: a real possibility in the future, with a real consequence if it happens.
coreIdea.es: El primer condicional te para en una bifurcación que realmente está más adelante: una posibilidad real en el futuro, con una consecuencia real si ocurre.

text.en: Formula: If + Present Simple, will + base verb. The 'if' clause names a real condition that could genuinely happen; the 'will' clause is the real consequence. Use it for predictions, promises, warnings, and on-the-spot decisions.
text.es: Fórmula: If + presente simple, will + verbo base. La cláusula 'if' nombra una condición real que de verdad podría pasar; la cláusula con 'will' es la consecuencia real. Se usa para predicciones, promesas, advertencias y decisiones tomadas en el momento.

text.en: Quick test: 'life in general' (always true) → Zero. 'Tomorrow, this weekend, if this happens' (one real future chance) → First.
text.es: Prueba rápida: 'la vida en general' (siempre cierto) → cero. 'Mañana, este fin de semana, si esto pasa' (una posibilidad real en el futuro) → primero.

text.en: Never put 'will' inside the 'if' clause. ❌ 'If it will rain, I'll take an umbrella.' The condition stays in Present Simple; only the result gets 'will'. ✅ 'If it rains, I'll take an umbrella.'
text.es: Nunca metas 'will' dentro de la cláusula 'if'. ❌ 'If it will rain, I'll take an umbrella.' La condición se queda en presente simple; solo el resultado lleva 'will'. ✅ 'If it rains, I'll take an umbrella.'

text.en: The result clause always needs 'will' too — don't drop it. ❌ 'If I study, I pass the exam' (sounds like a guaranteed Zero-Conditional fact). ✅ 'If I study, I'll pass the exam' — a real, one-time prediction.
text.es: La cláusula de resultado también necesita 'will' siempre — no la quites. ❌ 'If I study, I pass the exam' (suena a un hecho garantizado del condicional cero). ✅ 'If I study, I'll pass the exam' — una predicción real, de una sola vez.

examples.en: If it rains, I'll take an umbrella.
examples.es: Si llueve, llevaré un paraguas.

examples.en: If you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus.
examples.es: Si no te apuras, perderás el bus.

examples.en: If she calls, I'll tell her the news.
examples.es: Si ella llama, le contaré la noticia.

examples.en: If we finish early, we'll go for a coffee.
examples.es: Si terminamos temprano, iremos por un café.

examples.en: If you touch that wire, you'll get a shock.
examples.es: Si tocas ese cable, te vas a electrocutar.

title.es: Segundo condicional — la postal del universo paralelo

coreIdea.en: The Second Conditional sends you a postcard from a parallel universe — one where the present or future is different from real life, purely imagined.
coreIdea.es: El segundo condicional te manda una postal de un universo paralelo — uno donde el presente o el futuro es distinto a la vida real, puramente imaginado.

text.en: Formula: If + Past Simple, would + base verb. The past tense doesn't mean past time here — it means distance from reality. You're describing an imaginary present or future: dreams, hypotheses, advice, opinions.
text.es: Fórmula: If + pasado simple, would + verbo base. El pasado aquí no significa tiempo pasado — significa distancia de la realidad. Estás describiendo un presente o futuro imaginario: sueños, hipótesis, consejos, opiniones.

text.en: Giving advice: 'If I were you, I'd...' — 'were' is the classic, safest form for 'I/he/she/it' in this structure (informal speech also allows 'was', but 'were' is the standard choice).
text.es: Para dar consejos: 'If I were you, I'd...' — 'were' es la forma clásica y más segura para 'I/he/she/it' en esta estructura (en habla informal también se oye 'was', pero 'were' es la opción estándar).

text.en: Never put 'would' inside the 'if' clause. ❌ 'If I would have more money, I would travel.' The imagined condition stays in Past Simple; only the result gets 'would'. ✅ 'If I had more money, I would travel.'
text.es: Nunca metas 'would' dentro de la cláusula 'if'. ❌ 'If I would have more money, I would travel.' La condición imaginada se queda en pasado simple; solo el resultado lleva 'would'. ✅ 'If I had more money, I would travel.'

text.en: Quick test: 'Do I believe this will really happen?' Yes → First Conditional. No, I'm just imagining → Second Conditional.
text.es: Prueba rápida: '¿Creo que esto realmente va a pasar?' Sí → primer condicional. No, solo lo estoy imaginando → segundo condicional.

examples.en: If I had more money, I would travel the world.
examples.es: Si tuviera más dinero, viajaría por el mundo.

examples.en: If I were you, I'd apologize.
examples.es: Si yo fuera tú, me disculparía.

examples.en: If she spoke French, she could get that job.
examples.es: Si ella hablara francés, podría conseguir ese trabajo.

examples.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?
examples.es: ¿Qué harías si te ganaras la lotería?

examples.en: If I didn't have to work, I would sleep all day.
examples.es: Si no tuviera que trabajar, dormiría todo el día.

title.en: Third Conditional — the sealed door to yesterday
title.es: Tercer condicional — la puerta sellada de ayer

coreIdea.en: The Third Conditional stands you in front of a sealed door to yesterday: you can only imagine what was behind it, because the past is locked and nothing can change it now.
coreIdea.es: El tercer condicional te pone frente a una puerta sellada de ayer: solo puedes imaginar qué había detrás, porque el pasado está sellado y ya nada puede cambiarlo.

text.en: Formula: If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle. This is the grammar of regret: an imaginary past that never happened, used for missed opportunities, criticism, and 'what if' speculation about history — nothing here can actually be changed.
text.es: Fórmula: If + pasado perfecto, would have + participio pasado. Es la gramática del arrepentimiento: un pasado imaginario que nunca ocurrió, usado para oportunidades perdidas, críticas, y especulación tipo '¿y si...?' sobre la historia — aquí nada se puede cambiar de verdad.

text.en: Quick test: 'Can I still change this situation?' Yes, it's still open → Second Conditional. No, it's finished, sealed in the past → Third Conditional.
text.es: Prueba rápida: '¿Todavía puedo cambiar esta situación?' Sí, sigue abierta → segundo condicional. No, ya terminó, sellada en el pasado → tercer condicional.

text.en: Never put 'would have' inside the 'if' clause. ❌ 'If I would have known, I would have told you.' The sealed-past condition needs Past Perfect ('had known'); only the result gets 'would have'. ✅ 'If I had known, I would have told you.'
text.es: Nunca metas 'would have' dentro de la cláusula 'if'. ❌ 'If I would have known, I would have told you.' La condición del pasado sellado necesita pasado perfecto ('had known'); solo el resultado lleva 'would have'. ✅ 'If I had known, I would have told you.'

text.en: Past Perfect needs the past participle, not the simple past. ❌ 'If she had came earlier, she wouldn't have missed the train.' ✅ 'If she had come earlier...'
text.es: El pasado perfecto necesita el participio pasado, no el pasado simple. ❌ 'If she had came earlier, she wouldn't have missed the train.' ✅ 'If she had come earlier...'

examples.en: If I had known you were coming, I would have cooked dinner.
examples.es: Si hubiera sabido que venías, habría cocinado la cena.

examples.en: If she had studied medicine, she would have become a doctor.
examples.es: Si ella hubiera estudiado medicina, se habría convertido en médica.

examples.en: If they had left earlier, they wouldn't have missed the flight.
examples.es: Si hubieran salido más temprano, no habrían perdido el vuelo.

examples.en: If I hadn't broken my leg, I would have run the marathon.
examples.es: Si no me hubiera roto la pierna, habría corrido el maratón.

examples.en: Would you have forgiven him if he had apologized?
examples.es: ¿Lo habrías perdonado si él se hubiera disculpado?

title.es: Condicionales mixtos — el dominó que viaja en el tiempo

coreIdea.en: A Mixed Conditional is a domino that falls in one time period and knocks over a domino standing in a completely different one — a past cause with a present result, or a present truth with a past result.
coreIdea.es: Un condicional mixto es un dominó que cae en una época y tumba a otro dominó parado en una época completamente distinta — una causa pasada con resultado presente, o una verdad presente con resultado pasado.

text.en: There are two patterns. Type 1 — Past cause, present result: If + Past Perfect, would + base verb ('If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now'). Type 2 — Present situation, past result: If + Past Simple, would have + past participle ('If I were more organised, I would have remembered the meeting').
text.es: Hay dos patrones. Tipo 1 — causa pasada, resultado presente: If + pasado perfecto, would + verbo base ('If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now'). Tipo 2 — situación presente, resultado pasado: If + pasado simple, would have + participio pasado ('If I were more organised, I would have remembered the meeting').

text.en: Quick test: 'Does the consequence happen now, or did it happen in the past?' Now → Type 1 (past cause / present result). In the past → Type 2 (present situation / past result).
text.es: Prueba rápida: '¿La consecuencia pasa ahora, o pasó en el pasado?' Ahora → tipo 1 (causa pasada / resultado presente). En el pasado → tipo 2 (situación presente / resultado pasado).

text.en: Don't force a pure Third Conditional onto a sentence where the result is clearly true right now. ❌ 'If I had studied medicine, I would have been a doctor' (sounds like a one-time attempt that's over). If the point is 'and that's why I'm NOT a doctor today', the result needs the present form: ✅ 'I would be a doctor now.'
text.es: No fuerces un tercer condicional puro en una frase donde el resultado es claramente cierto ahora mismo. ❌ 'If I had studied medicine, I would have been a doctor' (suena a un intento único ya terminado). Si el punto es 'y por eso NO soy médico hoy', el resultado necesita la forma presente: ✅ 'I would be a doctor now.'

examples.en: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
examples.es: Si hubiera estudiado medicina, sería médico ahora.

examples.en: If I were more organised, I would have remembered the meeting.
examples.es: Si fuera más organizado, habría recordado la reunión.

examples.en: If she hadn't moved to Canada, she wouldn't be fluent in French now.
examples.es: Si ella no se hubiera mudado a Canadá, no hablaría francés con fluidez ahora.

examples.en: If he weren't so shy, he would have asked her out years ago.
examples.es: Si él no fuera tan tímido, la habría invitado a salir hace años.

examples.en: If we hadn't missed the flight, we would be on the beach right now.
examples.es: Si no hubiéramos perdido el vuelo, estaríamos en la playa en este momento.

title.en: Wish & If Only — the complaint genie
title.es: Wish e If Only — el genio de las quejas

coreIdea.en: 'Wish' is a genie who only grants complaints: it never talks about the future you want, only the present or past you don't like — and 'if only' is the same genie shouting louder.
coreIdea.es: 'Wish' es un genio que solo concede quejas: nunca habla del futuro que quieres, solo del presente o pasado que no te gusta — e 'if only' es el mismo genio pero gritando más fuerte.

topics.source: General English grammar reference (extends the backshift logic taught for Second/Third Conditionals in the source PDFs; wish/if only is not itself covered by those PDFs).

text.en: I wish + Past Simple talks about a present situation you'd like to be different (dissatisfaction now): 'I wish I spoke English fluently' (I don't). Don't confuse this with 'hope', which IS about the future you want.
text.es: I wish + pasado simple habla de una situación presente que te gustaría que fuera distinta (insatisfacción ahora): 'I wish I spoke English fluently' (no lo hablo). No confundas esto con 'hope', que SÍ habla del futuro que quieres.

text.en: I wish + Past Perfect talks about a past situation you regret — the same 'sealed door' logic as the Third Conditional: 'I wish I had studied harder' (I didn't, and it's over).
text.es: I wish + pasado perfecto habla de una situación pasada que lamentas — la misma lógica de la 'puerta sellada' del tercer condicional: 'I wish I had studied harder' (no lo hice, y ya pasó).

text.en: I wish + would + base verb complains about someone else's annoying behaviour (not about yourself): 'I wish you would stop interrupting me.' 'If only' works the same way as 'wish', just more emotional and emphatic.
text.es: I wish + would + verbo base se queja del comportamiento molesto de otra persona (no de ti mismo): 'I wish you would stop interrupting me.' 'If only' funciona igual que 'wish', solo que más emotivo y enfático.

text.en: Never use 'wish' + Present Simple to mean 'I want'. ❌ 'I wish I have more time' (sounds like a literal translation of 'ojalá tenga'). The verb after 'wish' backshifts, just like the Second/Third Conditional: ✅ 'I wish I had more time.'
text.es: Nunca uses 'wish' + presente simple para decir 'quiero'. ❌ 'I wish I have more time' (suena a una traducción literal de 'ojalá tenga'). El verbo después de 'wish' retrocede un tiempo, igual que en el segundo/tercer condicional: ✅ 'I wish I had more time.'

examples.en: I wish I spoke English fluently.
examples.es: Ojalá hablara inglés con fluidez.

examples.en: I wish I had studied harder for that exam.
examples.es: Ojalá hubiera estudiado más para ese examen.

examples.en: I wish you would stop interrupting me.
examples.es: Ojalá dejaras de interrumpirme.

examples.en: If only I had more free time.
examples.es: Si tan solo tuviera más tiempo libre.

examples.en: If only she hadn't quit her job.
examples.es: Si tan solo ella no hubiera renunciado a su trabajo.

title.en: Unless & Friends — the spice rack of conditions
title.es: Unless y sus amigos — el especiero de las condiciones

coreIdea.en: 'If' is the plain salt of conditions — unless, provided that, as long as, even if, in case and whether are the spice rack: same basic dish, different flavour and formality.
coreIdea.es: 'If' es la sal básica de las condiciones — unless, provided that, as long as, even if, in case y whether son el especiero: el mismo plato de fondo, pero con sabor y formalidad distintos.

text.en: 'Unless' means 'if...not' — it names the one thing that would block the result. 'Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train' = 'If you don't hurry, you'll miss the train.'
text.es: 'Unless' significa 'si...no' — nombra lo único que bloquearía el resultado. 'Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train' = 'If you don't hurry, you'll miss the train.'

text.en: 'Provided that' and 'providing (that)' are formal/business ('only if this requirement is met'); 'as long as' is the everyday, conversational version of the same idea; 'on condition that' is even more formal, typical of contracts.
text.es: 'Provided that' y 'providing (that)' son formales/de negocios ('solo si se cumple este requisito'); 'as long as' es la versión cotidiana y conversacional de la misma idea; 'on condition that' es aún más formal, típica de contratos.

text.en: 'Even if' means the result does NOT change no matter what — the opposite logic of plain 'if'. 'In case' is not the same as 'if': it means 'because this MIGHT happen' — a precaution, not a condition ('Take an umbrella in case it rains' ≠ 'Take an umbrella if it rains'). 'Whether...or...' presents two alternatives where the outcome doesn't depend on which one happens.
text.es: 'Even if' significa que el resultado NO cambia sin importar qué pase — la lógica contraria de un 'if' normal. 'In case' no es lo mismo que 'if': significa 'porque esto PODRÍA pasar' — una precaución, no una condición ('Take an umbrella in case it rains' ≠ 'Take an umbrella if it rains'). 'Whether...or...' presenta dos alternativas donde el resultado no depende de cuál ocurra.

text.en: The classic double-negative trap: because 'unless' already means 'if...not', never add another negative after it. ❌ 'Unless you don't study, you'll fail' (this actually means the opposite of what most students intend). ✅ 'Unless you study, you'll fail.'
text.es: La trampa clásica de la doble negación: como 'unless' ya significa 'si...no', nunca le agregues otra negación. ❌ 'Unless you don't study, you'll fail' (esto en realidad dice lo contrario de lo que casi todos quieren decir). ✅ 'Unless you study, you'll fail.'

examples.en: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train.
examples.es: A menos que te apures, perderás el tren.

examples.en: You can borrow my car provided that you fill up the tank.
examples.es: Puedes tomar prestado mi carro siempre que llenes el tanque.

examples.en: I'll go to the party as long as you come with me.
examples.es: Iré a la fiesta siempre y cuando vengas conmigo.

examples.en: Even if it rains, we're going hiking.
examples.es: Aunque llueva, vamos a caminar por la montaña.

examples.en: Take your ID in case they ask for it.
examples.es: Lleva tu identificación por si te la piden.

title.es: Inversión formal — la oración de esmoquin

coreIdea.en: Formal inversion is a conditional sentence putting on a tuxedo: drop 'if', swap the subject and auxiliary, and the whole sentence sounds dressed up for a business email, a contract, or literature.
coreIdea.es: La inversión formal es una oración condicional poniéndose un esmoquin: se quita 'if', se intercambian el sujeto y el auxiliar, y toda la frase suena elegante, lista para un correo de negocios, un contrato o literatura.

text.en: In formal English, you can drop 'if' and invert the subject with an auxiliary instead: 'Should' (Should you need any assistance... = If you need...), 'Were' (Were I you... = If I were you...), 'Had' (Had I known... = If I had known...). The meaning doesn't change — only the register does.
text.es: En inglés formal, puedes quitar 'if' e invertir el sujeto con un auxiliar: 'Should' (Should you need any assistance... = If you need...), 'Were' (Were I you... = If I were you...), 'Had' (Had I known... = If I had known...). El significado no cambia — solo el registro.

text.en: You'll meet this in business emails, legal contracts, academic writing, and literature — not in everyday spoken conversation. Using plain 'if' is never wrong; inversion is an optional upgrade.
text.es: Lo vas a encontrar en correos de negocios, contratos legales, escritura académica y literatura — no en la conversación cotidiana. Usar un 'if' normal nunca está mal; la inversión es un adorno opcional.

text.en: Don't keep 'if' AND invert at the same time — pick one. ❌ 'If should you need assistance...' Either 'If you need assistance...' or 'Should you need assistance...', never both together.
text.es: No dejes 'if' Y inviertas al mismo tiempo — elige uno. ❌ 'If should you need assistance...' Es 'If you need assistance...' o 'Should you need assistance...', nunca los dos juntos.

text.en: Match the auxiliary to the conditional type: 'Should' replaces First-Conditional 'if' (real future possibility); 'Were' replaces Second-Conditional 'if' (imaginary present); 'Had' replaces Third-Conditional 'if' (sealed past).
text.es: Haz coincidir el auxiliar con el tipo de condicional: 'Should' reemplaza el 'if' del primer condicional (posibilidad real futura); 'Were' reemplaza el del segundo (presente imaginario); 'Had' reemplaza el del tercero (pasado sellado).

examples.en: Should you need any assistance, please contact reception.
examples.es: Si necesita cualquier asistencia, por favor contacte a recepción.

examples.en: Were I in your position, I would accept the offer.
examples.es: Si yo estuviera en tu posición, aceptaría la oferta.

examples.en: Had I known about the delay, I would have booked an earlier flight.
examples.es: Si hubiera sabido sobre el retraso, habría reservado un vuelo más temprano.

examples.en: Should the client cancel, a full refund will be issued.
examples.es: Si el cliente cancela, se emitirá un reembolso completo.

examples.en: Had she arrived on time, she wouldn't have missed the introduction.
examples.es: Si ella hubiera llegado a tiempo, no se habría perdido la introducción.

prompt.en: If you heat water, it ___ (a scientific fact).
prompt.es: If you heat water, it ___ (un hecho científico).

why.en: Zero Conditional describes a fact that's always true — no future tense needed. 'If you heat water, it boils,' every time, guaranteed.
why.es: El condicional cero describe un hecho siempre cierto — no necesita futuro. 'If you heat water, it boils,' siempre, garantizado.

prompt.en: If you mix blue and yellow, you ___ (get) green.
prompt.es: If you mix blue and yellow, you ___ (get) green.

why.en: Present Simple in both halves: mixing these colors always produces green — a fixed rule of color, not a prediction.
why.es: Presente simple en ambas partes: mezclar estos colores siempre produce verde — una regla fija del color, no una predicción.

prompt.en: Plants die if they ___ (not/get) water.
prompt.es: Plants die if they ___ (not/get) water.

why.en: Even in the 'if' clause with a negative condition, Zero Conditional stays present: 'don't get', not 'won't get' — the rule never shifts to future.
why.es: Incluso en la cláusula 'if' con condición negativa, el condicional cero se queda en presente: 'don't get', no 'won't get' — la regla nunca cambia a futuro.

prompt.en: Which sentence correctly follows workplace safety instructions (Zero Conditional)?
prompt.es: ¿Cuál oración sigue correctamente las instrucciones de seguridad (condicional cero)?

items.answer: If the alarm rings, everyone leaves the building.
distractors: If the alarm will ring, everyone leaves the building.
If the alarm rings, everyone will leave the building.

why.en: Instructions and rules use Zero Conditional: both halves present, no 'will' anywhere — the rule always applies the same way.
why.es: Las instrucciones y reglas usan el condicional cero: ambas mitades en presente, sin 'will' en ninguna parte — la regla siempre aplica igual.

prompt.en: If people don't sleep enough, they ___ (get) irritable.
prompt.es: If people don't sleep enough, they ___ (get) irritable.

why.en: A general truth about human behaviour — Present Simple in both halves, no future needed.
why.es: Una verdad general sobre el comportamiento humano — presente simple en ambas partes, sin necesidad de futuro.

prompt.en: If it ___ tomorrow, I'll take an umbrella.
prompt.es: If it ___ tomorrow, I'll take an umbrella.

why.en: The 'if' clause never takes 'will' — the condition itself stays in Present Simple, even though we're talking about tomorrow.
why.es: La cláusula 'if' nunca lleva 'will' — la condición se queda en presente simple, aunque hablemos de mañana.

prompt.en: If you don't hurry, you ___ (miss) the bus.
prompt.es: If you don't hurry, you ___ (miss) the bus.

why.en: The result of a real future possibility needs 'will' (or 'll) — it's a genuine warning, not a general fact.
why.es: El resultado de una posibilidad real en el futuro necesita 'will' (o 'll) — es una advertencia genuina, no un hecho general.

prompt.en: Which sentence is a real prediction about tomorrow's exam?
prompt.es: ¿Cuál oración es una predicción real sobre el examen de mañana?

items.answer: If I study tonight, I'll pass the exam.
distractors: If I study tonight, I pass the exam.
If I will study tonight, I'll pass the exam.

why.en: 'I pass' (no will) sounds like a guaranteed Zero-Conditional fact; 'If I will study' puts 'will' in the wrong clause. Only 'If I study..., I'll pass' is correct First Conditional.
why.es: 'I pass' (sin will) suena a un hecho garantizado del condicional cero; 'If I will study' pone 'will' en la cláusula equivocada. Solo 'If I study..., I'll pass' es el primer condicional correcto.

prompt.en: Warn a friend: touching that wire → an electric shock. Use First Conditional.
prompt.es: Advierte a un amigo: tocar ese cable → una descarga eléctrica. Usa el primer condicional.

items.answer: If you touch that wire, you'll get a shock.
accept: If you touch that wire, you'll get a shock.
If you touch that wire, you will get a shock.

why.en: A real warning about a real possible action: condition in Present Simple, consequence with 'will'.
why.es: Una advertencia real sobre una acción realmente posible: condición en presente simple, consecuencia con 'will'.

prompt.en: Someone says 'I'm cold.' You reply with a spontaneous decision:
prompt.es: Alguien dice 'I'm cold.' Tú respondes con una decisión espontánea:

items.answer: If you're cold, I'll close the window.
distractors: If you're cold, I close the window.
If you're cold, I'm closing the window.

why.en: A real, spontaneous decision made right now needs 'will' in the result — 'I close' sounds like a habit/fact, and 'I'm closing' sounds like an action already in progress, not a fresh decision.
why.es: Una decisión real y espontánea tomada en el momento necesita 'will' en el resultado — 'I close' suena a hábito/hecho, y 'I'm closing' suena a una acción ya en curso, no a una decisión nueva.

prompt.en: If I ___ more money, I would travel the world.
prompt.es: If I ___ more money, I would travel the world.

why.en: The 'if' clause never takes 'would' — the imagined condition stays in Past Simple ('had'), even though we mean right now, not the past.
why.es: La cláusula 'if' nunca lleva 'would' — la condición imaginada se queda en pasado simple ('had'), aunque hablemos de ahora, no del pasado.

prompt.en: If I ___ you, I'd apologize right away.
prompt.es: If I ___ you, I'd apologize right away.

why.en: 'If I were you' is the standard, safest form for giving advice — 'am' breaks the imaginary-distance pattern, and 'would be' puts 'would' in the wrong clause.
why.es: 'If I were you' es la forma estándar y más segura para dar consejos — 'am' rompe el patrón de distancia imaginaria, y 'would be' pone 'would' en la cláusula equivocada.

prompt.en: If she ___ (speak) French, she could get that job.
prompt.es: If she ___ (speak) French, she could get that job.

why.en: An imagined present ability (she doesn't speak French) needs Past Simple in the 'if' clause — distance from reality, not past time.
why.es: Una habilidad presente imaginada (ella no habla francés) necesita pasado simple en la cláusula 'if' — distancia de la realidad, no tiempo pasado.

prompt.en: Which sentence correctly imagines an alternate life?
prompt.es: ¿Cuál oración imagina correctamente una vida alterna?

items.answer: If I didn't have to work, I would sleep all day.
distractors: If I wouldn't have to work, I would sleep all day.
If I don't have to work, I would sleep all day.

why.en: 'Wouldn't' never belongs in the 'if' clause, and 'don't' (Present Simple) breaks the imaginary distance — 'didn't' (Past Simple) is what signals 'this isn't real.'
why.es: 'Wouldn't' nunca va en la cláusula 'if', y 'don't' (presente simple) rompe la distancia imaginaria — 'didn't' (pasado simple) es lo que marca 'esto no es real.'

prompt.en: What ___ (you/do) if you won the lottery?
prompt.es: What ___ (you/do) if you won the lottery?

why.en: Asking about an imaginary future event uses 'would' in the question too — 'What would you do if...' is the standard hypothetical question pattern.
why.es: Preguntar sobre un evento futuro imaginario también usa 'would' en la pregunta — 'What would you do if...' es el patrón estándar de pregunta hipotética.

prompt.en: If I ___ you were coming, I would have cooked dinner.
prompt.es: If I ___ you were coming, I would have cooked dinner.

why.en: The 'if' clause needs Past Perfect ('had known'), never 'would have' — and plain Past Simple ('knew') isn't strong enough to seal this as unchangeable history.
why.es: La cláusula 'if' necesita pasado perfecto ('had known'), nunca 'would have' — y el pasado simple ('knew') no es suficiente para sellar esto como historia inmodificable.

prompt.en: If she ___ earlier, she wouldn't have missed the train.
prompt.es: If she ___ earlier, she wouldn't have missed the train.

why.en: Past Perfect uses the past participle: 'come', not the simple-past form 'came'. ❌ 'had came' is a very common mixing of the two past forms.
why.es: El pasado perfecto usa el participio pasado: 'come', no la forma de pasado simple 'came'. ❌ 'had came' es una mezcla muy común de las dos formas de pasado.

prompt.en: If they had left earlier, they ___ (not/miss) the flight.
prompt.es: If they had left earlier, they ___ (not/miss) the flight.

why.en: The result of an imaginary, unchangeable past needs 'would have' + past participle — a consequence that never actually happened.
why.es: El resultado de un pasado imaginario e inmodificable necesita 'would have' + participio pasado — una consecuencia que nunca ocurrió en realidad.

prompt.en: Express regret: you broke your leg, so you didn't run the marathon. Use Third Conditional.
prompt.es: Expresa arrepentimiento: te rompiste la pierna, por eso no corriste el maratón. Usa el tercer condicional.

items.answer: If I hadn't broken my leg, I would have run the marathon.
accept: If I hadn't broken my leg, I would have run the marathon.
If I had not broken my leg, I would have run the marathon.

why.en: A sealed, unchangeable past: the negative condition needs Past Perfect ('hadn't broken'), the result needs 'would have' + participle.
why.es: Un pasado sellado e inmodificable: la condición negativa necesita pasado perfecto ('hadn't broken'), el resultado necesita 'would have' + participio.

prompt.en: Would you have forgiven him if he ___ ?
prompt.es: Would you have forgiven him if he ___ ?

why.en: The 'if' clause of a question in Third Conditional still needs Past Perfect ('had apologized'), never 'would have', and plain Past Simple isn't strong enough to mark this unchangeable past.
why.es: La cláusula 'if' de una pregunta en tercer condicional todavía necesita pasado perfecto ('had apologized'), nunca 'would have', y el pasado simple no es suficiente para marcar este pasado inmodificable.

prompt.en: If I had studied medicine, I ___ a doctor now.
prompt.es: If I had studied medicine, I ___ a doctor now.

why.en: 'Now' signals the result is a present state — use 'would be', not 'would have been' (which would push the result into the past too).
why.es: 'Now' marca que el resultado es un estado presente — usa 'would be', no 'would have been' (que empujaría el resultado también al pasado).

prompt.en: If I ___ more organised, I would have remembered the meeting.
prompt.es: If I ___ more organised, I would have remembered the meeting.

why.en: The cause here is a present, ongoing trait ('I'm not organised'), so the 'if' clause uses Past Simple ('were'), not Past Perfect — only the result reaches back into the past.
why.es: La causa aquí es un rasgo presente y constante ('no soy organizado'), así que la cláusula 'if' usa pasado simple ('were'), no pasado perfecto — solo el resultado se mete en el pasado.

prompt.en: If she hadn't moved to Canada, she ___ (not/be) fluent in French now.
prompt.es: If she hadn't moved to Canada, she ___ (not/be) fluent in French now.

why.en: Past cause ('hadn't moved'), present result ('now') — the result stays in the present form 'wouldn't be', not 'wouldn't have been'.
why.es: Causa pasada ('hadn't moved'), resultado presente ('now') — el resultado se queda en la forma presente 'wouldn't be', no 'wouldn't have been'.

prompt.en: Combine: you missed a flight in the past; because of that, you are not on the beach right now. Use a Mixed Conditional.
prompt.es: Combina: perdiste un vuelo en el pasado; por eso, no estás en la playa en este momento. Usa un condicional mixto.

items.answer: If we hadn't missed the flight, we would be on the beach right now.
accept: If we hadn't missed the flight, we would be on the beach right now.
If we had not missed the flight, we would be on the beach right now.

why.en: Past cause (Past Perfect: 'hadn't missed') + present result (would + base verb: 'would be') — the domino that fell yesterday still knocks something over today.
why.es: Causa pasada (pasado perfecto: 'hadn't missed') + resultado presente (would + verbo base: 'would be') — el dominó que cayó ayer todavía tumba algo hoy.

prompt.en: If he ___ (not/be) so shy, he would have asked her out years ago.
prompt.es: If he ___ (not/be) so shy, he would have asked her out years ago.

why.en: The cause is a present, ongoing personality trait ('he's shy'), so the 'if' clause uses Past Simple ('weren't'), even though the missed result is in the past.
why.es: La causa es un rasgo de personalidad presente y constante ('él es tímido'), así que la cláusula 'if' usa pasado simple ('weren't'), aunque el resultado perdido esté en el pasado.

prompt.en: I wish I ___ English fluently (but I don't).
prompt.es: I wish I ___ English fluently (but I don't).

why.en: 'Wish' about a present dissatisfaction backshifts the verb to Past Simple, just like Second Conditional — 'speak' (Present) would wrongly sound like a literal translation of 'ojalá hablo'.
why.es: 'Wish' sobre una insatisfacción presente retrocede el verbo a pasado simple, igual que el segundo condicional — 'speak' (presente) sonaría como una mala traducción literal de 'ojalá hablo'.

prompt.en: I wish I ___ (study) harder for that exam.
prompt.es: I wish I ___ (study) harder for that exam.

why.en: Regret about a finished, sealed past needs Past Perfect after 'wish' — the same logic as the Third Conditional.
why.es: El arrepentimiento sobre un pasado terminado y sellado necesita pasado perfecto después de 'wish' — la misma lógica del tercer condicional.

prompt.en: I wish you ___ interrupting me all the time.
prompt.es: I wish you ___ interrupting me all the time.

why.en: Complaining about someone else's repeated, annoying behaviour uses 'wish' + would — 'stopped' sounds like a one-time regret and 'stop' is simply wrong here.
why.es: Quejarse del comportamiento repetido y molesto de otra persona usa 'wish' + would — 'stopped' suena a un lamento de una sola vez y 'stop' simplemente está mal aquí.

prompt.en: Express a stronger, more emotional wish about not having enough free time. Use 'If only'.
prompt.es: Expresa un deseo más fuerte y emotivo sobre no tener suficiente tiempo libre. Usa 'If only'.

items.answer: If only I had more free time.
accept: If only I had more free time.

why.en: 'If only' works exactly like 'wish' but sounds more emphatic and emotional — the same backshifted Past Simple for a present complaint.
why.es: 'If only' funciona igual que 'wish' pero suena más enfático y emotivo — el mismo pasado simple retrocedido para una queja presente.

prompt.en: You have a flight tomorrow and you genuinely believe good weather is possible. Which sentence fits?
prompt.es: Tienes un vuelo mañana y de verdad crees que el buen clima es posible. ¿Cuál oración corresponde?

items.answer: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
distractors: I wish it didn't rain tomorrow.

why.en: 'I wish it didn't rain' sounds like a literal translation of 'ojalá no lloviera', but 'wish' is reserved for things that ARE true or unlikely — a realistic hope about a real future event needs 'hope', not 'wish'.
why.es: 'I wish it didn't rain' suena a una traducción literal de 'ojalá no lloviera', pero 'wish' se reserva para cosas que SÍ son ciertas o poco probables — una esperanza realista sobre un evento futuro real necesita 'hope', no 'wish'.

prompt.en: ___ you hurry, you'll miss the train.
prompt.es: ___ you hurry, you'll miss the train.

why.en: The result 'you'll miss the train' only makes sense with the negative-condition word: 'Unless you hurry' = 'If you don't hurry'. Plain 'If you hurry' would (wrongly) mean hurrying causes you to miss it.
why.es: El resultado 'you'll miss the train' solo tiene sentido con la palabra de condición negativa: 'Unless you hurry' = 'If you don't hurry'. Un 'If you hurry' normal (incorrectamente) diría que apurarse hace que lo pierdas.

prompt.en: Which sentence correctly warns a student about failing?
prompt.es: ¿Cuál oración advierte correctamente a un estudiante sobre reprobar?

distractors: Unless you don't study, you'll fail.

why.en: 'Unless' already contains a hidden 'not' ('if...not'), so adding 'don't' creates a double negative that flips the meaning. ❌ 'Unless you don't study' actually means 'if you don't study, you won't fail' — the opposite of the warning.
why.es: 'Unless' ya contiene un 'not' escondido ('si...no'), así que agregar 'don't' crea una doble negación que invierte el significado. ❌ 'Unless you don't study' en realidad dice 'si no estudias, no reprobarás' — lo contrario de la advertencia.

prompt.en: ___ (even/if) it rains, we're going hiking — nothing will stop us.
prompt.es: ___ (even/if) it rains, we're going hiking — nothing will stop us.

why.en: 'Even if' signals that the result stays exactly the same no matter what happens with the condition — unlike plain 'if', where the result depends on the condition.
why.es: 'Even if' señala que el resultado se mantiene igual sin importar qué pase con la condición — a diferencia de un 'if' normal, donde el resultado sí depende de la condición.

prompt.en: Take your ID ___ they ask for it at the door (it's just a precaution).
prompt.es: Take your ID ___ they ask for it at the door (it's just a precaution).

why.en: 'In case' means 'because this might happen' — you carry the ID as a precaution whether or not they actually ask. 'If they ask for it' would (wrongly) suggest you only bring it after knowing they'll ask.
why.es: 'In case' significa 'porque esto podría pasar' — llevas la identificación como precaución sin importar si te la piden o no. 'If they ask for it' (incorrectamente) sugeriría que solo la llevas después de saber que te la van a pedir.

prompt.en: You'll get a full refund ___ you keep the receipt (a formal business condition).
prompt.es: You'll get a full refund ___ you keep the receipt (una condición formal de negocios).

why.en: 'Provided that' means the refund is guaranteed ONLY when this requirement is met. 'Even if' says the opposite logic — it would (wrongly) promise the refund no matter what, even without the receipt.
why.es: 'Provided that' significa que el reembolso está garantizado SOLO si se cumple este requisito. 'Even if' tiene la lógica contraria — prometería (incorrectamente) el reembolso sin importar qué, incluso sin el recibo.

prompt.en: ___ you need any assistance, please contact reception (formal).
prompt.es: ___ you need any assistance, please contact reception (formal).

why.en: 'Should' inverted with the subject formally replaces 'If you need...' — no 'if' is needed once you invert, and 'would' is the wrong auxiliary for a real future possibility.
why.es: 'Should' invertido con el sujeto reemplaza formalmente 'If you need...' — no necesitas 'if' una vez que inviertes, y 'would' es el auxiliar equivocado para una posibilidad real futura.

prompt.en: ___ (were/I) in your position, I would accept the offer (formal).
prompt.es: ___ (were/I) in your position, I would accept the offer (formal).

why.en: Formal inversion of Second Conditional swaps 'If I were' for 'Were I' — the imaginary distance from reality stays, just dressed up.
why.es: La inversión formal del segundo condicional cambia 'If I were' por 'Were I' — la distancia imaginaria de la realidad se mantiene, solo más elegante.

prompt.en: Which is the correct formal inversion of 'If I had known about the delay, I would have booked an earlier flight'?
prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la inversión formal correcta de 'If I had known about the delay, I would have booked an earlier flight'?

items.answer: Had I known about the delay, I would have booked an earlier flight.
distractors: Had I know about the delay, I would have booked an earlier flight.
If had I known about the delay, I would have booked an earlier flight.

why.en: The inverted auxiliary 'Had' still needs the past participle 'known' (not 'know'), and 'if' must disappear completely once you invert.
why.es: El auxiliar invertido 'Had' todavía necesita el participio pasado 'known' (no 'know'), y 'if' debe desaparecer por completo una vez que inviertes.

prompt.en: Which sentence correctly upgrades 'If the client cancels, a full refund will be issued' to formal inversion?
prompt.es: ¿Cuál oración convierte correctamente 'If the client cancels, a full refund will be issued' a inversión formal?

items.answer: Should the client cancel, a full refund will be issued.
distractors: If should the client cancel, a full refund will be issued.

why.en: You either keep 'if' or invert with 'should' — never both. ❌ 'If should the client cancel...' mixes the two registers into an error.
why.es: O te quedas con 'if' o inviertes con 'should' — nunca los dos juntos. ❌ 'If should the client cancel...' mezcla los dos registros en un error.
